I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father grew wheat and maize on this same ground, and I do the same. I know nothing else, and at my age I am not going to learn something new. My two sons help me during the busy periods — planting and harvest — but the decisions are mine.

I have about 5 mu of land I still work myself. The rest I have let my eldest son manage. 5 mu is enough for an old man.

In autumn I plant winter wheat. I always do. We need the wheat flour at home, and I sell what is left over. I will buy the improved seed from the village supply station — the government recommends it and the village head says it yields better. I do not know the variety name exactly but I will ask at the station.

For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before sowing — phosphorus and potassium mixed with some nitrogen — then I top-dress urea at jointing. I probably use more fertilizer than the technicians say I should, but in my experience the soil here is hungry and I do not want to lose the harvest. I irrigate three times: at sowing if it is dry, at jointing, and at heading. Water is getting harder to pump — the well is deeper every year — but wheat needs water.

After wheat harvest in June I plant maize directly into the stubble. No ploughing — I hire the machine to direct seed. Maize is easier. Hybrid seed, one or two irrigations if there is no rain, one fertilizer application. By October it is done.

That is my year. Always has been.
